_note: Rules for the guard and the drafter. NO prospect data lives here. Every number below is a PLACEHOLDER, not a researched figure (see docs/research-agenda.md, G7 and G8). Tune them from the pilot, not from a guess.

pilot._note: PRD E1. Accounts the pipeline created cannot be researched until a principal records a pilot pass: at least minAccounts fully reviewed accounts and zero fabrications. 10 is the PRD's floor, not a researched number.

banned.ai_voice: AI-generated voice calls are treated as artificial-voice calls under U.S. telemarketing rules and are not used for outbound. A person places calls.
banned.ringless_voicemail: Ringless voicemail is treated as a call under U.S. telemarketing rules and is not used. A person leaves voicemail after dialing.
banned.sms: No text messages: no consent, wrong channel for this audience.
banned.whatsapp: No WhatsApp: no consent, wrong channel for this audience.

sec._note: SEC EDGAR access for the CMBS adapter (PRD E4-S2). The SEC asks automated clients to name themselves with a contact (fair access policy [verify current wording]) and to stay under 10 requests a second; 150 ms between requests keeps well under. userAgent is a [CONFIRM] placeholder until a principal fills it (PRD Q11): firm name and a monitored contact email, e.g. "Firm Name ops@firm-domain". knownSpecialServicers is the reviewed list of special servicer firm names; a name the distribution report shows that is not on it is flagged in the run notes, never guessed. Seeded with the ten firm names that appeared as special servicer on distribution-report covers in the 2026-11-13 runs. A name matches when it directly follows the label, compared without case or punctuation, so "LNR Partners" covers "LNR Partners, LLC", "LNR Partners,LLC" and "LNR Partners, Inc.". A principal should review the list; add a firm only after checking it.

fdic._note: FDIC loan-sale announcements on www.fdic.gov (PRD E16-S2, outbound sources run fdicsales). Gentle by design: requests are at least minIntervalMs apart (20 s, so three a minute), or further if robots.txt sets a longer Crawl-delay, and only paths robots.txt allows are read. At most maxEvents sale pages per run; an announcement PDF is read once, when it is new or its link changes, and at most maxPdfBytes of it. userAgent is a [CONFIRM] placeholder until a principal fills it: the firm's name and a monitored BUSINESS contact, e.g. "Firm Name ops@firm-domain". The run refuses while it is a placeholder, and refuses an email address at a personal domain (personalDomains below).

enforcement._note: Enforcement orders (PRD next-five E18-S2, outbound sources run enforcement). The Federal Reserve's action files only, for now. Every value is a PLACEHOLDER for a principal to review. minIntervalMs: at least this long between requests (www.federalreserve.gov sets no Crawl-delay; robots.txt answered 404 on 2026-11-16). maxDocsPerRun: order documents read per run, for orders that name a bank in the universe; each is read once. maxPdfBytes: the most of one order PDF read. minShare: a file holding fewer actions than this share of the last run's count fails the run, so a truncated file never stands in for the record. reviewWindowDays: how far back an unmatched order is put on the review list (outbound enforcement unmatched). flags: the fixed phrases looked for in an order's text; only which appear is stored, never the text. userAgent: optional; while it is a placeholder, requests send no custom User-Agent. If a principal fills it, the firm's name and a monitored business contact.

fdic._note: FDIC orders (outbound sources run fdicorders), run on a principal's machine with Playwright: the monthly enforcement releases on www.fdic.gov, then each release's order list on orders.fdic.gov, read in a headless browser. PLACEHOLDERS. minIntervalMs: at least this long between requests (www.fdic.gov's Crawl-delay of 1 second wins if longer). backfillMonths: how far back the first run reads releases. maxReleasesPerRun: release lists captured per run, oldest first. maxPages: pages of one list followed through its Next button. timeoutMs: the most one page may take to load.

occ._note: OCC orders (outbound sources run occorders, and the monthly sources.enforcement job): the OCC's monthly news release 'OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for <Month>', found by walking the year's release numbers. PLACEHOLDERS. backfillYears: how many past years the first run reads (each about 100 releases). maxMisses: release numbers answering 404 in a row before a year is taken as read to its end (gaps of 2 were seen). maxRequestsPerRun: a cap; the next run continues. minIntervalMs: at least this long between requests.

mergers._note: Merger applications (PRD next-five E18-S3, outbound sources run mergerapps): the Federal Reserve's weekly H.2 release, one page per district. PLACEHOLDERS. districts: the Reserve Bank districts read each week; all twelve, since a bank in our metros can be acquired by a holding company anywhere. backfillWeeks: how far back the first run reads. maxWeeksPerRun: weeks read per run (each week is 14 requests). minIntervalMs: at least this long between requests. minRowsPerWeek: a week with fewer filings across the districts is noted in the run log. userAgent: optional, as for enforcement. gapLeadDays: PLACEHOLDER; outbound mergers gap counts only closes from this many days after the first H.2 week read, since an application is filed months before its close (Q5, decided 2026-11-16: accept the gap and count it).

counties._note: County records watchers (docs/county-loans.md; county-data-build-vs-buy 3.4 and 5.2, component 9). Each county's adapter is registered in src/counties.mjs; a county is watched once a principal lists its source id in watch, after its robots.txt and terms are read and dated (D-B8) and its decision is recorded in sources.json. Caldwell County, TX (tx-caldwell-notices-of-sale) is watched from 2026-11-18, on a principal's decision of that date; the worker reads every watched county each Monday (job loans.watch). userAgent: the firm's name and a monitored business contact, sent with every request. minIntervalMs: at least this long between requests to a county host (the county playbook's 3 a minute); a source's own pacing (Caldwell: 21 seconds) or a longer Crawl-delay in robots.txt wins. maxBytes: the most of one list page read. maxDocumentBytes: the most of one linked document (a scanned notice) read. maxDocumentsPerRun: the most linked documents fetched in one run; the rest wait for the next. backfillDays: on a source's first run, only documents its list dates within this many days are read; older ones are recorded as history and never fetched. freshDays: the verify check fails when a source's last good run is older. PLACEHOLDERS for a principal to review.

parcels._note: The property behind each county filing, from the county's own parcel record (docs/county-loans.md 3a, src/parcels.mjs). By a principal's ruling of 2026-11-23, only a filing whose parcel the assessor classes commercial, multifamily of 5 or more units, or commercial land is a lead; every other filing is out (a home) or on the property-not-confirmed list. Only Jefferson has a parcel source: the Assessor's public parcel layer, CC BY 4.0, attributed wherever a property type shows. The weekly run (loans.watch) looks up each new or changed filing after reading its county; a lookup that fails is counted and never fails the county's run. enabled false turns every lookup off. minIntervalMs: the least time between requests to a parcel host, never less than the adapter's 1.5 seconds.

sources._note: Each registered real county source, by id (src/counties.mjs), with whether it may run. enabled is false until a principal has recorded the decision the adapter's terms carry (terms.decision 'allowed', with the date and who decided); runNoticeSource refuses a source marked false, and nothing is fetched. waitingOn says what it waits on. The weekly job (loans.watch) reads every enabled source: each one listed in watch that is not marked false here, and each one marked true here.

tx-caldwell-notices-of-sale.decided: A principal's decision of 2026-11-18, recorded in sources.json (principalDecision): weekly, lender-level use only, no individual named in a notice contacted, the disclaimer rechecked monthly.

jefferson.decided: A principal's decision of 2026-11-18: Jefferson's GTS reports (the NED report and the pre-sale list) may be read weekly by software. The watcher stores extracted fields only, never the county's PDFs; the county's copyright claim in data compilations goes to counsel (D-B9).

douglas.decided: A principal's decision of 2026-11-18: the firm accepts the Douglas reports page's terms (lawful and ethical use only, a release of liability), so the pre-sale list may be read weekly by software. The watcher stores extracted fields only.

sales._note: The who-sells-to-whom ledger (PRD E16, outbound sales build). filingSearches: the saved searches in filings.json whose hit on a bank's filing counts as a disclosed sale (8-K Item 2.01, a completed acquisition or disposition of assets, may also be the bank BUYING: the event says so). acquisitionKinds: the FDIC structure-event kinds that count as a whole-bank acquisition; affiliate-reorganization (224, inside one holding company) is left out, as in scoring.json. Both lists are PLACEHOLDERS for a principal to review.

outcomes._note: PRD E15-S4, the outcomes report. PLACEHOLDERS. Below minToTune confirmed call outcomes, the report says the counts are too few to tune scoring weights on. leadTimeBucketsDays are the edges of the lead-time groups, from an account's first signal to its first meeting. The report never changes weights; a principal does.

market._note: PRD next-five E20, the market data pack (outbound market pack). The disclosure guard (D-M3, decided 2026-11-16: these strict defaults). minInstitutions: a bank figure needs at least this many banks; maxShare: no one bank (or one CMBS loan) may be more than this share of a figure; minLoans, minTrusts, minServicers: a CMBS figure needs at least this many loans, distinct trusts and distinct special servicers. Complementary suppression follows. Left out (D-M2, decided): failures, FDIC loan sales, implied recoveries. Publishing waits for counsel (Q25); when it publishes, it is a data section in the news desk's monthly Hotel loan watch, widened to multifamily and retail, under the firm's name (D-M1, decided).

intermediaries._note: PRD next-five E19 (outbound intermediaries ...). kinds: the intermediary kinds in scope (D-I1, decided 2026-11-16: loan-sale advisors and CMBS special servicers; receivers and counsel wait for county records). weights: the ranking (D-I3, decided 2026-11-16: PLACEHOLDERS, a principal tunes them after reading the first ranked list); each component earns weight x min(value / full, 1): metroMandates (mandates in our metros), sectorMandates (in buy-box sectors), namedSellers (distinct sellers a source names; an unknown seller never counts), recentMandates (each mandate worth 0.5^(age in months / halfLifeMonths)), balance (dollars where a source gives one). reminderDays: a buyer-list re-certification due within this many days shows on the Status page. Registrations and proof of funds are owned by Josh (D-I2, decided); proof of funds waits for the credibility package (research agenda D9).

backtest._note: PRD E17, the backtest of the score (outbound backtest panel, labels, run, report). Every value is a PLACEHOLDER for a principal to set, except those marked decided (2026-11-14: the window, holdout, eras, horizons, universe and label kinds). window: the as-of quarter-ends replayed (its own _note). callReportLagDays: a quarter's Call Report counts as known only from quarter-end plus this many days (FDIC asks banks to file within 30 days; 60 allows for its publishing). sodReleaseLagDays: the Summary of Deposits as of June 30 counts as known only from June 30 plus this many days, its release date [verify: FDIC publishes no release date in the API; the 2026 data's search index was built on 2026-09-18]. minCoverage: every as-of quarter needs Call Report rows for at least this share of its universe, or the panel run is suspect. minLabels: below this many labelled banks a figure says 'too few to tune on' (D-B4). holdout: what is held out for the final test, declared before any comparison (D-B5, decided 2026-11-14: by bank, a third, fixed by its seed; see its own _note). eras: the periods every report shows apart, so a pooled figure is never read alone (Q6, decided). topK: the size of the headline group, ranked by distress and timing points only. horizonQuarters: how many quarters after the as-of date a label counts for the headline (D-B1, decided: 4). horizonsReported: the horizons shown side by side in each report (D-B1, decided: 2, 4 and 8). universe: banks headquartered in metros.json hqStates plus every bank with a Summary of Deposits branch in the six metros (D-B3; every US bank is not built). labelKinds: the label kinds that count (D-B2); disclosed_sale is listed but stays off and is reported unavailable until the SEC contact (Q11) and confirmed filers exist; merger (ordinary mergers) is off unless listed here; enforcement_order waits for E18-S2.

window._note: Decided 2026-11-14 (Q6): 2006 to 2026, so the 2009-2012 failures are in (70 in our five states, against 5 since 2019). The panel also pulls scoring.json lookbackQuarters before the first; every scored field is filled from 2001. Read the eras apart.

holdout._note: Decided 2026-11-14 (Q5, D-B5): hold out banks, not quarters, so every era keeps labels on both sides. A bank is held out when the hash of seed:CERT falls below share. The seed is declared here before any comparison and must not change; changing it is shown on every later report as a moved holdout. by: quarter (with from) is still built.
